The stepper the owner presses sits at viewport y578/y780/y660/y660 - on screen at every width - and the .b-undo plate that names the change and carries the Undo control lands at document y2263/y2310/y1911/y1911 with viewport heights 844/1024/900/960. It is 1419px, 1286px, 1011px and 951px below the fold, and the page grows 123px/70px/70px/70px as it arrives, so the footer moves under the person who just acted. It is not taste: the single surface that reports a reversible change is unreachable at the moment it has something to say, at every breakpoint. Confirmed. On the head-to-head the panel asked for: the reserved-44px-band-in-the-rail proposal is the WEAKER of the two. Its distinctive part does not buy what it claims - the reflow is cured by WHERE the plate goes, not by reserving space for it, because in either the rail or the editor the plate grows a sticky column or a fixed sheet rather than the page under the owner's hands - and it costs the design its stated silence rule (render-b.js:271-273 and b.css:488, 504: empty until it has something true to say), planting a permanently visible empty box in the one column another finding already faults as 609px of dead space. It is also only half a fix: .b-stick is sticky ONLY at min-width 1280 (b.css:738), so below that the plate would sit in static flow above the measure and scroll away, which is why the finding has to invent a second bottom-pinned layer - stacked directly on top of .b-edit, which below 1280 is already position:fixed; bottom:12px; z-index:3; max-height:72dvh (b.css:403-409). Two fixed layers fighting for the bottom 12px of a 390px screen is a worse trade than the defect. Moving the bar inside the editor is better on placement at every width for free: the editor is already in the sticky rail at 1280+ (measured at viewport y546, right under the steppers) and already a fixed bottom sheet at 390/768 (measured at y464/y667), so one reparent puts the report beside the control that made it with no new layer, no reserved band and the silence rule intact. Its one genuine loss is persistence: closeEditor removes .b-edit (render-b.js:452-456) and both Done (:502) and Escape (:525) fire it while history is non-empty, whereas the Ctrl+Z handler is bound at root (:534-541) and stays live - so the owner who nudges a moment, presses Done, then reconsiders would keep the capability and lose the only named route to it. That loss is narrow and closable; the reserved band's mobile hole is not. Neither proposal should ship as written.
sharpenedFix: Keep exactly one .b-undo node - the gate asserts count === 1 (interaction-check.mjs:414) and wireOwner binds its click once at wire time (render-b.js:543), and both survive reparenting. Keep display:none while data-empty="true"; reserve nothing. Two placements for the one node. (1) While the editor exists: in openEditor (render-b.js:471-477) append the node as the last child of .b-edit, after the .b-editActs row. At 1280+ that puts it in the sticky rail directly beneath the steppers that produced it; below 1280 it rides inside the fixed bottom sheet. Nothing above it moves when it fills, because .b-edit is display:grid and grows downward inside its own box. (2) While no editor is open: in closeEditor (render-b.js:452), before removing .b-edit, return the node to its present position in .b-field, and give it position:sticky; bottom:12px; z-index:2 in b.css:490 so that whenever it has something to say it rides the bottom edge of the viewport instead of the bottom of a 2124px page. Because it is display:none when empty it occupies nothing at rest and adds no band. This costs one CSS declaration plus two appendChild lines, keeps the wording, the role="status" live region and the Ctrl Z legend untouched, adds no colour, weight or family, and closes the Done-then-reconsider gap that pure editor-nesting would open.
